title: The memory store: an append-only log of item versions on files or PostgreSQL, notes and lessons read where they live
request: The owner: continue the memory plan non-stop; 35.2 stores the items 35.1's contract defines.
spec: MEMORY_PLAN.md 35.2: a MemoryStore protocol with a file store and a PostgreSQL store (migration 0022); readers, not copies, for project notes and accepted lessons; migrate and backup cover it; the store's keepers archive it. Done when the same calls pass on files and PostgreSQL, a note appears as a fact without being written twice, and deleting a project retires its items in the product view and keeps them in the store.
plan: Read the lessons store (file and PostgreSQL behind one protocol), the storage models, a table-creating migration with an append-only trigger, the migration tool and project deletion.
Build the store as a log of versions (the last version of an id is its state, retirement final), the readers, the deletion hook and the migration step.
Test the same behaviour on both stores, the readers, the deletion and the migration; review; fix; record; commit.

decisions.decision: The store is an append-only log of versions, not a table of current rows
decisions.why: the owner's rule that the store keeps what is deleted; a retirement or a counter moved is a new version, and the database refuses an update or a delete by trigger

decisions.decision: Project notes and lessons are read where they live, never copied into the store
decisions.why: one source of truth each; an item's id is its words, so a note read twice is one item, and a deleted project's notes simply stop being read

decisions.decision: Memory versions are filed in the store under the kind lessons use
decisions.why: a memory item is the same sort of record as a workspace lesson; a new kind would change the core's store contract for no gain

decisions.decision: The events of writing and retiring move to 35.3, and playbook bullets with the screen for read items to 35.4
decisions.why: 35.3 builds the writing path where events belong; 35.4 builds the brief, the last door before an agent reads an item

change: dclab_rnd/memory/__init__.py (FileMemory, PgMemory, latest, open_memory, remember, retire_scope, view) and readers.py (from_project, from_lessons, line, author); storage/models.py and migration 0022 (memory_item_version, append-only); storage/migrate.py (the versions moved in one transaction and checked); experience/retention.py (a deleted project's stored items retired); store/keepers database.py and standard.py; tests/test_memory_store.py and test_storage_migrate.py.

findings.defect: The store's code was written before its tests
findings.scenario: the package skill asks for a failing test first; the store and readers were written, then the tests
findings.cause: the shape was copied from the lessons store and felt known
findings.fix: the tests were written to cover each behaviour on both stores, and the review then found ten problems the tests had not
findings.impact: tests written after the code tend to check what the code does rather than what the plan asks

findings.defect: The deletion test failed on PostgreSQL
findings.scenario: the suite run with --pg: the test wrote through the file store while deletion opened the database store, so nothing was retired
findings.cause: the test named the file store directly
findings.fix: the test writes through open_memory, so it checks deletion on whichever store the workspace has
findings.impact: the nightly full gate on PostgreSQL would have failed

findings.defect: After a crash cut a line, the next saved write was lost too
findings.scenario: a line cut without its line break; the next write was appended to it, so both lines were unreadable, though the write had been flushed and returned as stored
findings.cause: the append did not check how the file ended
findings.fix: under the lock, a missing final line break is written before the new line
findings.test: test_a_damaged_line_is_skipped_never_fatal now cuts the line without a break
findings.impact: a remembered fact silently lost after any crash

findings.defect: A note removed and written again with the same words never showed
findings.scenario: a removed note and a later active note with the same words share an id; the removed one, read as retired, hid the other for good
findings.cause: removed notes were read as retired items, and retirement is final for an id
findings.fix: removed notes are not read at all, and a retired stored copy never hides an item read where it lives

findings.defect: remember stored retired words that would never be seen
findings.scenario: remember, retire, remember the same words: the call succeeded and the item stayed hidden forever
findings.cause: an id is its words and retirement is final
findings.fix: remember refuses words whose item is retired, asking for a correction in other words

findings.defect: The migration could copy memory partly and never finish
findings.scenario: version 7 of 10 fails; the next run sees six rows and copies nothing, and verify did not compare memory
findings.cause: one transaction a version, and no check
findings.fix: every version in one transaction, and verify compares the counts
findings.test: test_storage_migrate checks two versions copied once

findings.defect: Memory in the database was not archived by the store
findings.scenario: the database keeper's lists did not name the table, so database memory never reached the store; the folder fell under 'other'
findings.cause: a new table and folder need their keepers
findings.fix: the table in the append-only list with its claim, and a class for the memory folder
findings.impact: the owner's rule that the store keeps everything broken for memory

findings.defect: Writes and retirements made no event
findings.scenario: the plan's rules ask an event for every write and retirement; a deletion recorded only a count
findings.cause: events belong to the writing path
findings.fix: moved to 35.3 in the plan, retirements included
findings.open: until 35.3, a retirement shows only as a count in the deletion's audit record

findings.defect: Deleting any project made an empty memory folder
findings.scenario: forget on a fresh file workspace left memory/ behind
findings.cause: the file store made its folder when opened
findings.fix: the folder is made by the first write; deletion skips a file workspace with no memory

findings.defect: The file lock held within one process only
findings.scenario: the API and the worker are two processes: a write between retire_scope's read and its writes stayed active after the delete
findings.fix: the repository's file lock, as the ledger uses, between processes too

findings.defect: Any author named like 'user…' was read as a person
findings.scenario: 'username' or 'user_agent_bot' became a person, who may write a correction
findings.fix: only the authors studio notes and reviews write for a person

outcome: The memory store is built and reviewed: versions kept forever on files or PostgreSQL, the same calls on both, notes and lessons read where they live, a deleted project's items retired, the migration and the store's keepers covering it. Ten review findings fixed or moved on in the plan, the most serious a test that failed on PostgreSQL and a write lost after a crash.
lessons: Run a storage test in both modes before calling it done: a test that names one backend checks only that one.
An append after a crash must first end the cut line, or the next good write is lost with it.
When an id is its words and retirement is final, decide what writing the same words again means, and test it.
Write the tests first even when the shape is copied: here the review, not the tests, found the problems.
risks: A storage change needs the full gate on PostgreSQL.
Another session works in the same folder; the storage files are shared code.
